svg.title: From a nightly extract to an order the doctor signs
svg.desc: 1. Extract (ejecutar.py): Loads the list: insert-only, every date checked. Amparo · synthetic: eGFR 72 → 68 · ACR 85 in January. Real · NHANES: Woman, 60s · eGFR 105 · ACR 98 (median of 82 like her). 2. Signed rules (S1a · S1b · S3): SQL; thresholds in one table, signed by a physician. Amparo · synthetic: Not repeated for 10 months → S1b. Real · NHANES: ACR ≥ 30 on one visit → S1b, repeat ACR. 3. Note reader (Qwen3-4B → verificar.py): The model points to a sentence; the code checks it and reads the value and date. Amparo · synthetic: “sentence 2” → ACR 110, 12 Sep ✓. Real · NHANES: Not tested: NHANES has no notes. 4. Final rules (S1c): Two high ACRs ≥ 3 months apart → S1c. Already ordered → not listed. Amparo · synthetic: 85 → 110, 8 months apart → S1c. Real · NHANES: Not tested: no notes or orders in NHANES. 5. Doctor signs (ui/index.html): Reason, numbers, dates. Sign, or dismiss with a reason. Amparo · synthetic: 10:20 · consider a CKD code (N18). Real · NHANES: Prepared, not signed. 10 days later: ACR 31 (≥ 30). Across NHANES: 143 per 1,000 adults with diabetes or hypertension have urine albumin ≥ 30 mg/g behind an eGFR ≥ 60 (2021–2023). 52.4 % (95 % CI 44–61) of repeat-ACR orders were ≥ 30 again on a second urine within 10 days (2009–2010).

text.font-family: Inter, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

text.tspan: Every box is a real file or rule. Traced twice: Amparo (synthetic, with notes) and a real NHANES 2009–2010 participant (no notes).
